identity.question: Will three people dissent the December Fed decision?

literal_rule: Count dissenting votes on the Fed Funds Rate decision in the Dec 8-9, 2026 FOMC statement; exactly three = Yes, otherwise No. FOMC statement primary; credible reporting also permitted.

calendar.finding: 2026 calendar lists Dec 8-9; next meeting Oct 27-28. Page last modified Oct 7.

roster.note: Roster lists 12 current voting members and separates alternates. No vacancy shown on this page; Dec attendance, substitutions, recusal/abstention unknown.

latest_statement.finding: Policy rate raised 25bp to 3.75%-4.00%; 12-0, all 12 named members in favor, none against.

latest_minutes.finding: Minutes say all members agreed to the 25bp increase and reproduce the 12-0 roll call. Participant views/risks varied but are not mapped to individual December votes; alternates and other presidents are separately listed in attendance.

voting_members_recent_speeches.speaker: Christopher J. Waller
voting_members_recent_speeches.finding: If data as expected, anticipates more hikes; timing flexible, not necessarily consecutive. Personal view, not vote commitment.

voting_members_recent_speeches.speaker: Philip N. Jefferson
voting_members_recent_speeches.finding: Voted for Sept increase; described activity/employment risks as balanced, inflation risk as upside, and said he would continue assessing data before judging policy. Personal view.

voting_members_recent_speeches.speaker: John C. Williams
voting_members_recent_speeches.finding: No urgency after Sept; if outlook holds, one more upward adjustment late 2026 may be appropriate. Conditional personal forecast, not vote commitment.
